prompt: Implement GridCopier.deepCopy(int[][] grid) so the returned grid shares NO arrays with the original: changing a cell in the copy must not touch the original, and vice versa.
explanation: In Java a 2D array is an outer array holding references to row arrays. A shallow copy (clone or arraycopy of the outer array) duplicates only those references, so both grids still point at the same rows and a write through one is visible through the other. A deep copy allocates a fresh row array for every index -- new int[grid[i].length] -- and copies the values, leaving the two grids with no shared objects at either level.
hints: Start with new int[grid.length][] -- an outer array whose rows are not allocated yet.
For each index i, allocate copy[i] = new int[grid[i].length] so jagged rows keep their own lengths.
Copy values with an inner loop (or java.util.Arrays.copyOf(grid[i], grid[i].length) per row).
